'''James F. Drake''' (born June 26, 1947) is an American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] who specializes in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11506033.html|title=Drake, James (James F.)|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> He is known for his studies on [[plasma instabilities]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Drake|first1=J. F.|last2=Kaw|first2=P. K.|last3=Lee|first3=Y. C.|last4=Schmid|first4=G.|last5=Liu|first5=C. S.|last6=Rosenbluth|first6=Marshall N.|date=1974|title=Parametric instabilities of electromagnetic waves in plasmas|journal=The Physics of Fluids|volume=17|issue=4|pages=778–785|doi=10.1063/1.1694789|bibcode=1974PhFl...17..778D|issn=0031-9171|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Drake|first1=J. F.|last2=Lee|first2=Y. C.|date=1977|title=Kinetic theory of tearing instabilities|journal=The Physics of Fluids|volume=20|issue=8|pages=1341–1353|doi=10.1063/1.862017|bibcode=1977PhFl...20.1341D|issn=0031-9171}}</ref> and [[magnetic reconnection]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Birn|first1=J.|last2=Drake|first2=J. F.|last3=Shay|first3=M. A.|last4=Rogers|first4=B. N.|last5=Denton|first5=R. E.|last6=Hesse|first6=M.|last7=Kuznetsova|first7=M.|last8=Ma|first8=Z. W.|last9=Bhattacharjee|first9=A.|last10=Otto|first10=A.|last11=Pritchett|first11=P. L.|date=2001|title=Geospace Environmental Modeling (GEM) Magnetic Reconnection Challenge|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics|language=en|volume=106|issue=A3|pages=3715–3719|doi=10.1029/1999JA900449|bibcode=2001JGR...106.3715B|issn=2156-2202|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Drake|first1=J. F.|last2=Swisdak|first2=M.|last3=Che|first3=H.|last4=Shay|first4=M. A.|date=2006|title=Electron acceleration from contracting magnetic islands during reconnection|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=443|issue=7111|pages=553–556|doi=10.1038/nature05116|pmid=17024088|bibcode=2006Natur.443..553D|s2cid=4427833 |issn=1476-4687}}</ref> for which he was awarded the 2010 [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] by the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=":0" />

== Early life and career ==
Drake studied at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), where he received his [[bachelor's degree]] in 1969 and received his doctorate in 1975. In 1977, he moved to the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]], where he has been a professor since 1987.

He dealt with laser-plasma interaction and plasma [[turbulence]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Price|first1=L.|last2=Swisdak|first2=M.|last3=Drake|first3=J. F.|last4=Cassak|first4=P. A.|last5=Dahlin|first5=J. T.|last6=Ergun|first6=R. E.|date=2016|title=The effects of turbulence on three-dimensional magnetic reconnection at the magnetopause|journal=Geophysical Research Letters|language=en|volume=43|issue=12|pages=6020–6027|doi=10.1002/2016GL069578|arxiv=1604.08172|bibcode=2016GeoRL..43.6020P|s2cid=119293728 |issn=1944-8007}}</ref> He is known for explaining the mechanisms of the [[Magnetic reconnection|rapid reconnection of magnetic field lines]] and the resulting [[Particle acceleration|particle accelerations]] in [[Astrophysical plasma|astrophysical plasmas]] (for example on the sun).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Drake|first1=J. F.|last2=Cassak|first2=P. A.|last3=Shay|first3=M. A.|last4=Swisdak|first4=M.|last5=Quataert|first5=E.|title=A Magnetic Reconnection Mechanism for Ion Acceleration and Abundance Enhancements in Impulsive Flares|date=2009|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|language=en|volume=700|issue=1|pages=L16–L20|doi=10.1088/0004-637X/700/1/L16|bibcode=2009ApJ...700L..16D|s2cid=45087759 |issn=1538-4357|doi-access=free}}</ref> In computer simulations with Amitava Bhattacharjee and Michael Hesse (NASA), he was able to demonstrate the explosive nature of the dynamics of the magnetic fields, for example in [[Solar flare|solar flares]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://terpconnect.umd.edu/~drake/news/ScienceTimes.html|title=Unlocking Secrets of Magnetic Fields' Power|website=terpconnect.umd.edu|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1986, Drake was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1986&unit_id=DPP&institution=University+of+Maryland|title=APS Fellow Archive|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> He was subsequently awarded the 2010 [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for "''pioneering investigations of [[plasma instabilities]] in magnetically-confined, astrophysical and laser-driven plasmas; in particular, explication of the fundamental mechanism of fast [[Magnetic reconnection|reconnection of magnetic fields]] in plasmas; and leadership in promoting plasma science''".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Drake&first_nm=James&year=2010|title=2010 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref> 

He also received a Senior US Research Scientist Award from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2020}}
